items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I received a cable from Willie Lewis, who was leading a band in Paris at a club called the "Che France" and he asked me if I would like to join the band.

ctx.x: But you didn't record anything at that point?
Well, a little later I did, with the Willie Lewis orchestra.
Yeah, the Willie Lewis orchestra did record there, that's right.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well, it was tendered by my having received a telegram from Willie Lewis, actually, in Paris, offering me the job, you know, if I would like to come to Paris and play with his orchestra.

ctx.x: Excuse me, 1935. This is after your final engagement in the U.S., which was with Willy Bryant, and you accepted an offer to join Willie Lewis’ band in Paris [France]. Do you remember how that offer was tendered, as they say?

Well, it was tendered by my having received a telegram from Willie Lewis, actually, in Paris, offering me the job, you know, if I would like to come to Paris and play with his orchestra. I don’t know how long it took me to think it over, but I decided I would like to do it, and I did.
Was traveling to Europe something you had had in the back of your mind previously, or was this sort of a new [unclear]?
